theorem2_observed_window_data_definition.tex_statement: For every observed-window case $C$, exactly one of the three displayed source representations is exhibited: there are $b,W$ with $C=\mathrm{zero}(b,W)$, or $b,T,h_E$ with $C=\mathrm{one}(b,T,h_E)$, or $b,T,h_M,h_E$ with $C=\mathrm{multi}(b,T,h_M,h_E)$.

lemma1_continuous_duration_first_report_.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{reportingRate}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{durationDensity}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, if $\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\,dt=1$, if $\mathrm{durationDensity}$ is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0,\infty)$, and if $t\mapsto\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\operatorname{noArrivalProb}(\mathrm{reportingRate},t)$ is integrable with respect to the same restricted measure, then $\operatorname{continuousDurationFirstReportProbability}(\mathrm{reportingRate},\mathrm{durationDensity})=\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\operatorname{firstReportProbability}(\mathrm{reportingRate},t)\,dt$.

lemma1_continuous_duration_observed_rate.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{incidentRate},\mathrm{reportingRate}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{durationDensity}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, if $\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\,dt=1$, if $\mathrm{durationDensity}$ is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0,\infty)$, and if $t\mapsto\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\operatorname{noArrivalProb}(\mathrm{reportingRate},t)$ is integrable with respect to the same restricted measure, then $\operatorname{continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate}(\mathrm{incidentRate},\mathrm{reportingRate},\mathrm{durationDensity})=\mathrm{incidentRate}\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\operatorname{firstReportProbability}(\mathrm{reportingRate},t)\,dt$.

lemma1_nonhomogeneous_first_report_proba.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{reportingRate},\mathrm{durationDensity}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, if $\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\,dt=1$, if $\mathrm{durationDensity}$ is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0,\infty)$, and if $t\mapsto\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\exp[-\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du]$ is integrable with respect to that measure, then $\operatorname{continuousDurationFirstReportProbabilityOfCumulativeIntensity}(t\mapsto\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du,\mathrm{durationDensity})=\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\bigl(1-\exp[-\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du]\bigr)\,dt$.

lemma1_nonhomogeneous_observed_rate_inte.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{incidentRate}\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{reportingRate},\mathrm{durationDensity}:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, if $\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\,dt=1$, if $\mathrm{durationDensity}$ is integrable with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to $[0,\infty)$, and if $t\mapsto\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\exp[-\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du]$ is integrable with respect to that measure, then $\operatorname{continuousDurationObservedIncidentRateOfCumulativeIntensity}(\mathrm{incidentRate},t\mapsto\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du,\mathrm{durationDensity})=\mathrm{incidentRate}\int_{[0,\infty)}\mathrm{durationDensity}(t)\bigl(1-\exp[-\int_0^t\mathrm{reportingRate}(u)\,du]\bigr)\,dt$.

lemma1_steady_state_duration_source_obse.tex_statement: For every source steady-state duration model $M$ containing a latent Poisson incident process, independent eventual-report marks, and the displayed duration-mixture retention probability, the observed count path is measurable, starts at zero almost surely, is almost-surely monotone, has independent increments, and each interval increment has Poisson mass function with rate $\operatorname{continuousDurationObservedIncidentRate}(M.\mathrm{incidentRate},M.\mathrm{reportingRate},M.\mathrm{durationDensity})$ times the interval length.

proposition1_steady_state_duration_sourc.tex_statement: For a probability duration density and a positive observed rate for which the first-report probabilities at reporting rates $1$ and $2$ are positive, there exist two source steady-state duration models with distinct positive reporting rates, the same observed incident rate, almost-sure unit-window count averages converging to that rate, and observed homogeneous-Poisson count-process laws at that common rate.

lemma2_forward_selected_start_exponentia.tex_statement: Let $\Omega$ be a measurable standard-Borel space, $P$ a probability measure, $M$ a forward source model consisting of a positive-rate iid exponential interarrival path and a Condition-1 selected start, and $u\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}$. For $P$-almost every first-report history, the conditional probability that the forward Poisson process has no jump on the interval of length $u$ after $M.\mathrm{selection.startTime}$ equals the exponential-rate-$M.\mathrm{rate}$ tail probability of $(u,\infty)$.

appendix_shifted_poisson_after_first_jum.tex_statement: \forall {\Omega : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace \Omega] [inst_1 : StandardBorelSpace \Omega] {P : Measure \Omega} [inst_2 : IsProbabilityMeasure P] (M : assumption_lemma2_forward_source_model \Omega P), ⇑(condDistrib postFirstReportTail firstReportTime P) =ᵐ[map firstReportTime P] ⇑(const NNReal (exponentialInterarrivalMeasure rate))

homogeneous_reporting_delay_mean_formula.tex_statement: \forall (rate : ℝ) (h_rate : 0 < rate), \int (x : ℝ), x ∂{ rate := rate, rate_pos := h_rate }.measure = 1 / rate

equation3_mle_formula.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{totalCount}\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathrm{totalExposure}\in\mathbb{R}$, if $\mathrm{totalExposure}\ne 0$, then $\operatorname{mleRate}(\mathrm{totalCount},\mathrm{totalExposure})=\mathrm{totalCount}/\mathrm{totalExposure}$, where the natural count is cast to a real number.

equation3_mle_global_logLikelihood_max.tex_statement: For every $\mathrm{totalCount}\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathrm{totalExposure},\mathrm{rate}\in\mathbb{R}$, if $\mathrm{totalCount}\ne 0$, $\mathrm{totalExposure}>0$, and $\mathrm{rate}>0$, then $\operatorname{poissonRateLogLikelihood}(\mathrm{totalCount},\mathrm{totalExposure},\mathrm{rate})\le\operatorname{poissonRateLogLikelihood}(\mathrm{totalCount},\mathrm{totalExposure},\operatorname{mleRate}(\mathrm{totalCount},\mathrm{totalExposure}))$.

equation5_poisson_regression_rate_formul.tex_statement: For every finite type $\mathrm{Feature}$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and every $\beta,\theta:\mathrm{Feature}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\operatorname{poissonRegressionRate}(\alpha,\beta,\theta)=\exp\!\left(\alpha+\sum_{j:\mathrm{Feature}}\beta(j)\theta(j)\right)$.

equation6_poisson_regression_likelihood_.tex_statement: For a finite feature type, $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $\beta,\theta: \mathrm{Feature}\to\mathbb R$, an ordered observed timeline $T$, a causal endpoint source model $M$ and its density presentation $D$, if $T.\mathrm{window.exposure}>0$, then the conditional likelihood at $\exp(\alpha+\sum_j\beta_j\theta_j)$ is the rate-free residual times $\operatorname{sourcePoissonPMF}(\exp(\alpha+\sum_j\beta_j\theta_j),T.\mathrm{window.exposure},T.\mathrm{count})$; the residual is independent of the rate argument.

equation33_nyc_preprocessing_endpoint_is.tex_statement: For every type $\Omega$, measurable space $m_\Omega$ on $\Omega$, filtration $\mathcal{F}$ indexed by $\mathbb{R}$, and functions $\mathrm{startTime},\mathrm{inspectionTime},\mathrm{workOrderTime}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, if all three functions are stopping times for $\mathcal{F}$, then $\omega\mapsto\min\{\min\{\mathrm{startTime}(\omega)+100,\mathrm{inspectionTime}(\omega)\},\mathrm{workOrderTime}(\omega)\}$ is also a stopping time for $\mathcal{F}$.

appendix_theorem2_eq8_causal_stopping_so.tex_statement: For an ordered finite jump timeline $T$, a causal stopping source model $M$, a density presentation $D$, and a positive rate and exposure, the conditional likelihood is the rate-free causal residual times $\operatorname{sourcePoissonPMF}(\mathrm{rate},T.\mathrm{window.exposure},T.\mathrm{count})$.
